note: Crash report v3 (#13379) is a native app's report: the iPhone and Mac apps' crashes as MetricKit hands them over on a later launch. The app posts a dump (below) to POST /api/playtest/app-crash, and the API makes the report from it with the codec and keeps it by bucket like every other report. Its frames carry no names: a frame is the binary and the frame's offset in it, `f BINARY +0xOFFSET`, and the `build` line is the UUID of the app's own binary, which names the dSYM that resolves its frames (coax/web/symbols.sh app-frame). The signature is the kind and the three innermost frames in the app's own binary, each BINARY+0xOFFSET (the three innermost of any binary when none is the app's). Offsets change with every build, so one bug in two builds lands in two buckets. A room's report stays v1 and a page's v2; `source app` is only ever v3.

lines.value: the end of the day MetricKit reported the crash in, Unix ms
the system's version as MetricKit names it
the name of the app's own binary
UUID OFFSET BINARY: a frame of the crashed thread, innermost first; the binary's UUID (dashes and either case allowed), the offset into the binary in decimal, the binary's name
VERSION (BUILD), the app's version and build number; ? when unknown
the UUID of the app's own binary, 32 lowercase hex digits; 0 when no frame is in it
the signal's name (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT...), EXC for a Mach exception with no signal, else crash
BINARY +0xOFFSET (the offset into the binary, lowercase hex); innermost first, at most 24
KIND|BINARY+0xOFFSET, up to three: the innermost frames in the app's own binary, or of any binary when none is; KIND|TEXT when there is no frame
